Let’s talk about something we all have, but never seem to have enough of—time. Chapter 9 is called The Gift of Time and the Art of Saying Goodbye.
You know, time is one of those things that, once it’s spent, you just can’t get it back. As days slowly turn into years, it hits us—life really is finite. And the older we get, the more we start wondering: how should we spend the time we have left? There’s also this subtle, quiet skill we need to pick up along the way—the art of letting go. That means saying goodbye to people, places, even dreams we once held close. I want to share a story. Picture an elderly man, after a long, rich life, facing the end with this deep sense of peace. In his final days, he wasn’t alone. He was surrounded by family, swapping stories, sharing laughter, and spending quiet moments just reflecting together. He talked openly about his regrets and his joys, and you know what he did? He urged his loved ones to treasure every second they had together. Most of us try to push thoughts of endings aside, right? Maybe we’re afraid of loss, or just don’t want to think about it. But here’s something to pay attention to—there’s a quiet wisdom in facing the truth that everything is temporary. Saying goodbye can hurt, sure, but it can also be beautiful. It’s a chance to express real love, deep gratitude, and even forgiveness. The real gift of time isn’t about how much we get—it’s about how deeply we live it. A single afternoon where you’re truly present with someone you care about? That can mean more than years spent together, half-distracted. So, the art of saying goodbye is really about honoring what’s been, letting go with some grace, and making space for whatever comes next. A lot of people cling to the past, scared to step into the future. But letting go doesn’t mean forgetting. It’s about carrying forward the lessons, the love, the memories, and still being open to what’s ahead. Here’s something most people miss—the way you spend your time actually reveals what you value most. Every day, in the small choices—how you show up, who you give your energy to, what you decide is worth your effort—that’s how your life is shaped. When it’s all said and done, it’s not about counting days. It’s about making your moments count.
